findings.title: Home page is indexable

findings.title: No author attribution detected
findings.message: https://www.deluxewindowcleaning.co.uk/soffit-fascia-gutter-cleaning/ has no machine-readable author. If a name is shown visually but only as unmarked text (or rendered from a client-side payload), AI assistants cannot reliably attribute it. Make authorship explicit with one of: <meta name="author">, a JSON-LD author field, rel="author", or itemprop="author".
findings.fixSnippet:
<meta name="author" content="Author Name" />

// or in JSON-LD:
"author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "Author Name" }

findings.title: Page is short on body text
findings.message: https://www.deluxewindowcleaning.co.uk/derbyshire/payment/ has 230 visible words. Pages under 300 words rarely surface in AI answers because there isn't enough context. If you want this page to be quoted, expand it. If it's a navigational or transactional page, ignore. (Plus 7 more pages with a milder version of this issue, counted proportionally in the score.)

findings.title: No <h1> heading on the page

findings.title: Only 43% of images have alt text

findings.title: Missing security headers: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy
findings.message: 0 of 4 recommended security headers are set. Adding Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy hardens the site against clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, and referrer leakage. Not an AI-citation factor, but a standard best-practice signal.

X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

contentFindings.title: No clear entity statement in the first 300 words
contentFindings.message: The home page never plainly says what the brand is within its opening 300 words. Add one sentence of the form "<Brand> is a <category> that <what it does> for <who>". AI assistants lean on this exact pattern when deciding how to describe and whether to cite you.
